output.summary: A deciduous hardwood tree native to the eastern United States, though its exact native range is uncertain, black locust has deeply furrowed bark and paired prickles that vary greatly between trees. It spreads through root suckers, sometimes forming dense colonies.
output.edibilityNote: In parts of Europe and Japan, flowers are fried or made into jam; reports call shelled seeds and young pods edible, though bark and leaves are toxic.
